questions.question: The average of Anwar's marks in seven subjects is 75. His average in six subjects excluding Science is 70. How many marks did he get in Science?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Science** marks = Original **Average** + (Difference in Average × Number of remaining subjects)

Difference in **Average** = 75 − 70 = 5

Marks in **Science** = 75 + (5 × 6)

Marks in **Science** = 75 + 30 = 105

**∴ The correct answer is 105 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average marks of **Anwar** in **7 subjects** = 75

Average marks in **6 subjects** (excluding **Science**) = 70

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = **Average** × **Number of observations**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a685b42c5dfafd9575b4379dffae698fcdc1e4982b00e41fcc16b102ba3a3069.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total marks in **7 subjects** = 75 × 7 = 525

⇒ Total marks in **6 subjects** = 70 × 6 = 420

⇒ Marks in **Science** = (Total marks in 7 subjects) − (Total marks in 6 subjects)

⇒ Marks in **Science** = 525 − 420 = 105

**∴ The correct answer is 105 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Group

The **Arithmetic Mean** or **Average** is calculated by dividing the sum of all values by the total number of values: Average = Σx ÷ n.

Effect of Exclusion

When a value is excluded, if the **Average** decreases, the excluded value must be greater than the original average. Excluded Value = (Old Average × Old Count) − (New Average × New Count).

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, the **Combined Average** = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The average price of three items of furniture is ₹15,255. If their prices are in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7, the price of the cheapest item (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total **ratio sum** = 3 + 5 + 7 = **15 units**.

Average ratio = 15 ÷ 3 = **5 units**.

Given **5 units** = **₹15,255** ⇒ 1 unit = **₹3,051**.

**Cheapest item** (3 units) = 3 × 3,051 = **₹9,153**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,153.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average price of **3 furniture items** = **₹15,255**

Ratio of their prices = **3 : 5 : 7**

**Formula Used:**

Total Value = **Average** × **Number of Observations**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8af62946d834d861c5bf96b3b1c1d78fcd1dae2776c6194afa7a9c7ab4b53887.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total price of all items = 15,255 × 3 = **₹45,765**

⇒ Let the prices be **3x**, **5x**, and **7x**

⇒ 3x + 5x + 7x = 45,765

⇒ 15x = 45,765

⇒ x = 45,765 ÷ 15

⇒ x = **3,051**

⇒ Price of the cheapest item = 3x = 3 × 3,051

⇒ Cheapest item price = **₹9,153**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,153.**

**__Additional Information__**

Concept of Average

The average is the sum of all values divided by the total count. **Sum = Average × Count**.

Ratio Distribution

To find a specific share from a ratio a:b:c, use: **Share = (Ratio Part ÷ Sum of Ratios) × Total Value**.

Weighted Average

When items have different weights/quantities, the weighted average is **(Σwᵢxᵢ) ÷ Σwᵢ**.

questions.question: The sum of 6 numbers is 288. Find their average.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **average** is the **sum** divided by the **count**.

Direct calculation: 288 ÷ 6 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **sum** of 6 numbers = 288

Total **quantity** (n) = 6

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71fe99c224a21ca69c7f4db2892f21ff28c308b7eec7e7db3ed21cf326125077.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average = 288 ÷ 6

⇒ Average = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the average is simply (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Effect of Operations on Average

If every number in a set is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant **k**, the **average** also changes by that same constant **k**.</p

questions.question: The average of eight numbers is 15. The average of five of these numbers is 18. The average of the remaining three numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Base **Average** of 8 numbers = 15.

**Deviation** for 5 numbers = 5 × (18 − 15) = +15.

To balance, **Net Deviation** for remaining 3 numbers must be −15.

Deviation per **remaining number** = −15 ÷ 3 = −5.

**Required Average** = 15 − 5 = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 8 **numbers** = 15, Average of 5 **numbers** = 18.

**Formula:** **Total Sum** = **Average** × **Count of numbers**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/701e32218588a8ee61ef02509b72bb4e2f82bda87b88e2a196e8e71832667865.png] 

⇒ **Total sum** of 8 numbers = 8 × 15 = 120

⇒ **Sum** of first 5 numbers = 5 × 18 = 90

⇒ **Sum** of remaining 3 numbers = 120 − 90 = 30

⇒ **Average** of remaining 3 numbers = 30 ÷ 3 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

The **arithmetic mean** or average is calculated as the Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Combined Average

If two groups have n₁ and n₂ elements with averages a₁ and a₂, the **combined average** = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Weighted Average Principle

The sum of **deviations** of all values from the average is always zero. This is the core of the **deviation method** shortcut.</p

questions.question: The average score of 50 students in a class test is 45. Later, it was found that in one instance, a score of 25 was wrongly recorded as 35, and in another instance, a score of 30 was wrongly recorded as 28. Find the actual average score of the class.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Net deviation** in sum = (Correct scores) − (Wrongly recorded scores)

Net deviation = (25 + 30) − (35 + 28) = 55 − 63 = **−8**

**Average correction** = Net deviation ÷ Number of students = −8 ÷ 50 = **−0.16**

**Actual Average** = 45 − 0.16 = 44.84

**∴ The correct answer is 44.84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total students = 50 | Initial Average = 45 | Wrong scores = 35, 28 | Correct scores = 25, 30

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42939e0b6310a1a4ae50c080bae142e0be2a5f7509df0a6813235a8eee904c3f.png] 

**Formula:** Actual Average = [ (Initial Average × N) − (Wrong Sum) + (Correct Sum) ] ÷ N

⇒ Total Initial Sum = 50 × 45 = 2250

⇒ Total Wrong Sum recorded = 35 + 28 = 63

⇒ Total Correct Sum to be recorded = 25 + 30 = 55

⇒ Correct Total Sum = 2250 − 63 + 55 = 2242

⇒ Actual Average = 2242 ÷ 50

⇒ Actual Average = 44.84

**∴ The correct answer is 44.84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Average

If every value in a data set is increased or decreased by a constant **k**, the **mean (average)** of the data set also increases or decreases by **k**.

Weighted Average

When two groups with different averages **A₁** and **A₂** and sizes **n₁** and **n₂** are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Correction Principle

New Average = Old Average + [ (Correct Value − Incorrect Value) ÷ Total Number of Items ]. This is the fastest way to solve entry-error problems.</p

questions.question: Gopal bought 51 books at ₹1,120 per book from one shop and 45 books at ₹920 per book from another. What is the average price (in ₹) he paid per book?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **assumed average** be **₹1,000**.

Deviation of Group 1 (51 books): 51 × (+120) = **+6,120**

Deviation of Group 2 (45 books): 45 × (−80) = **−3,600**

Net deviation = 6,120 − 3,600 = **+2,520**

Average deviation = 2,520 ÷ (51 + 45) = 2,520 ÷ 96 = **26.25**

Actual Average = 1,000 + 26.25 = **1,026.25**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,026.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity of books from **Shop 1** (n₁) = **51** | Price (p₁) = **₹1,120**

Quantity of books from **Shop 2** (n₂) = **45** | Price (p₂) = **₹920**

**Formula Used:**

**Average Price** = (Total Cost) ÷ (Total Quantity)

Average = (n₁p₁ + n₂p₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a59bd7b6527bb340092def3beba05dc9b0b7dfa69d6d6a544d2406234a9cb30.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total cost from Shop 1 = 51 × 1,120 = **₹57,120**

⇒ Total cost from Shop 2 = 45 × 920 = **₹41,400**

⇒ Total cost of all books = 57,120 + 41,400 = **₹98,520**

⇒ Total number of books = 51 + 45 = **96**

⇒ Average price = 98,520 ÷ 96

⇒ Average price = **₹1,026.25**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,026.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

It is the average where each observation is assigned a **weight** based on its importance or quantity. Formula: Aw = Σ(wᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σwᵢ.

Deviation Method for Averages

Instead of multiplying large numbers, assume a **mean** and calculate the **algebraic sum** of differences from that mean to find the correction.

Average Speed and Price Relationship

Average price/speed is not just the **arithmetic mean** of the individual prices/speeds unless the **quantities/times** are equal.

questions.question: The average weight of 7 boys of a group is 54 kg. When a new boy joined the group, the average weight increased by 2 kg. Find the weight of the new boy.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Weight of **new boy** = New Average + (Initial number of boys × Increase in average)

⇒ **New Average** = 54 + 2 = 56 kg

⇒ Weight = 56 + (7 × 2) = 56 + 14 = 70 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 70 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average weight of **7 boys** = 54 kg, Average increase = 2 kg.

**Formula:** Total Weight = Average × Number of persons

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76a02c74a9e980b7e8215abfa63826a4d1deb7da2ea990a30dc842f01a4af5bb.png] 

⇒ Total weight of **7 boys** = 7 × 54 = 378 kg

⇒ Total number of boys after 1 boy joins = 8

⇒ **New average weight** = 54 + 2 = 56 kg

⇒ Total weight of **8 boys** = 8 × 56 = 448 kg

⇒ Weight of the **new boy** = Total weight of 8 boys − Total weight of 7 boys

⇒ Weight of the new boy = 448 − 378 = 70 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 70 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For a series of consecutive numbers or an AP, the average is simply (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

Replacement Rule

Weight of New person = Weight of Removed person + (Total Number × Change in Average).</p

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 83, 17, 62, 87, 62, 96, 86, 92 and 90 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume a **base mean** of 80 and calculate deviations from it.

Deviations: (+3), (−63), (−18), (+7), (−18), (+16), (+6), (+12), (+10).

Sum of deviations = 3 − 63 − 18 + 7 − 18 + 16 + 6 + 12 + 10 = −45.

Net change in mean = −45 ÷ 9 = −5.

Actual Arithmetic Mean = 80 − 5 = 75.

**∴ The correct answer is 75.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given observations:** 83, 17, 62, 87, 62, 96, 86, 92, 90

**Formula Used:** Arithmetic Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/217234f91c0e04b71d07bd52dfc3350c96ee3764c410f0338ffc447e69fc119a.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Total number of observations (n) = 9

⇒ Sum of observations = 83 + 17 + 62 + 87 + 62 + 96 + 86 + 92 + 90

⇒ Sum of observations = 675

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 675 ÷ 9

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 75

**∴ The correct answer is 75.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median of Data

To find the **Median**, arrange data in ascending order: 17, 62, 62, 83, 86, 87, 90, 92, 96. The middle term (5th position) is 86.

Mode of Data

The **Mode** is the value that appears most frequently. In this set, 62 appears twice, so the Mode is 62.

Range

The **Range** is the difference between the maximum and minimum values: 96 − 17 = 79.</p

questions.question: What is the average of all the natural numbers from 1 to 17?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The average of the first **n natural numbers** is always the **middle term** of the series.

Shortcut formula for **Average** = (n + 1) ÷ 2

Substitute n = **17**:

Average = (17 + 1) ÷ 2 = 18 ÷ 2 = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A sequence of **Natural Numbers** from 1 to 17.

**Formula Used:** Average of an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d8027bc0198612a0311d000375d4eb35faeff92e6e4e1275d8fb48d19578011f.png] 

⇒ First Term (a) = 1

⇒ Last Term (l) = 17

⇒ Average = (1 + 17) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 18 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The total sum of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula: **Sₙ = n(n + 1) ÷ 2**.

Average of First n Even Numbers

The average of the first n even natural numbers (2, 4, 6...) is simply **(n + 1)**.

Average of First n Odd Numbers

The average of the first n odd natural numbers (1, 3, 5...) is exactly equal to **n**.

Middle Term Property

In any sequence with an **odd number of terms** in AP, the average is always the **absolute middle term**.</p

questions.question: The average price of three items of furniture is ₹15,015. If their prices are in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7, the price of the costliest item (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Average** of ratio parts = (3 + 5 + 7) ÷ 3 = 5 units.

Given **average price** = ₹15,015 ⇒ 5 units = ₹15,015.

Value of 1 unit = 15,015 ÷ 5 = ₹3,003.

Price of the **costliest item** (7 units) = 7 × 3,003 = ₹21,021.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹21,021.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of **three items** = ₹15,015 and their **price ratio** = 3 : 5 : 7.

**Formula Used:** Total Sum = Average × Number of items.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4fa2dddd28fbcfae5876af4992a22b4f251db5f6ce53049e9faec1ac11f9c6c.png] 

⇒ Total price of items = 15,015 × 3 = ₹45,045

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 3 + 5 + 7 = 15 units

⇒ 15 units = ₹45,045

⇒ 1 unit = 45,045 ÷ 15 = ₹3,003

⇒ Price of **costliest item** (7 units) = 7 × 3,003

⇒ Price = ₹21,021

**∴ The correct answer is ₹21,021.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Average and Total

The **sum of observations** is always equal to the **Average** × **Number of observations**.

Ratio to Value Conversion

To find the value of a specific part in a **ratio** a : b : c, use the formula: Value = (Total Sum ÷ (a + b + c)) × required ratio part.

Average of a Ratio

If items are in ratio a : b : c, their **average unit** is (a + b + c) ÷ 3. This can be directly equated to the **numerical average** to find the value of one unit.

questions.question: The sum of five numbers is 655. The average of the first two numbers is 77 and the third number is 129. Find the average of the remaining two numbers.
questions.solution:

Sum of first 2 numbers = 77 × 2 = 154

Sum of first 3 numbers = 154 + 129 = 283

Sum of remaining 2 numbers = 655 − 283 = 372

Average of remaining 2 numbers = 372 ÷ 2 = 186

**∴ The correct answer is 186.**

questions.question: If the average of four numbers is 40 and three of the numbers among four are 40, 42 and 55, what will be the fourth number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net deviation from the **average** (40) must be zero.

Deviations: (40 − 40) = 0; (42 − 40) = +2; (55 − 40) = +15.

Total deviation = 0 + 2 + 15 = +17.

To balance, **fourth number** deviation must be −17.

Fourth number = 40 − 17 = 23.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 4 numbers = 40; Three numbers are 40, 42, and 55.

**Formula Used:** Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bc1153af55494f97f987f638bfcf7b6fba2fcb148ceb372fed161f8bc495966.png] 

⇒ Total sum = 40 × 4 = 160

⇒ Sum of the three known numbers = 40 + 42 + 55 = 137

⇒ Fourth number = Total sum − Sum of three numbers

⇒ Fourth number = 160 − 137

⇒ Fourth number = 23

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Deviations

The sum of the **deviations** of all observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero. This property is used in the deviation method shortcut.

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For an **arithmetic progression (AP)**, Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2. This applies to consecutive integers, even numbers, or odd numbers.

Combined Average

If two groups have sizes n₁, n₂ and averages A₁, A₂, then the **combined average** = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: Mohan bought 51 books at ₹1,120 per book from one shop and 48 books at ₹900 per book from another. What is the average price (rounded off to two decimal places, in ₹) he paid per book?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **books** = 51 : 48 = 17 : 16

Assume **base price** = ₹900

Deviation for first part = 1120 − 900 = +220

Net deviation = (17 × 220) ÷ (17 + 16) = 3740 ÷ 33 = 113.33

**Average Price** = 900 + 113.33 = 1013.33

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1013.33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of books from first shop (n₁) = **51** | Price (x₁) = **₹1,120**

Number of books from second shop (n₂) = **48** | Price (x₂) = **₹900**

**Formula Used:**

**Weighted Average Price** = (Total Cost) ÷ (Total Number of Books)

Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8313df0fc6c4e01c5c88d44f677afa88ba13c70b4dc2372c973fa2627bbf3f17.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total books = 51 + 48 = **99**

⇒ Total cost = (51 × 1120) + (48 × 900)

⇒ Total cost = 57120 + 43200 = **₹100,320**

⇒ Average Price = 100320 ÷ 99

⇒ Average Price = 1013.3333...

⇒ **Average Price** ≈ ₹1013.33

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1013.33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

It is used when different groups have different importance or sizes. Formula: Aw = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + ... + wₙxₙ) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + ... + wₙ).

Deviation Method for Averages

Instead of multiplying large numbers, assume an arbitrary mean and find the net deviation divided by total frequency to adjust the assumed mean.

Rounding Off Rules

When rounding to two decimal places, if the third decimal is 5 or more, round up the second decimal; otherwise, keep it the same.

questions.question: The average of 36 numbers is 45. If two numbers 37 and 53 are discarded, find the average of the remaining numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Initial Average** of 36 numbers = 45.

**Sum** of discarded numbers = 37 + 53 = 90.

**Average** of the two discarded numbers = 90 ÷ 2 = 45.

If the average of the **discarded items** is equal to the **group average**, the average of the **remaining items** does not change.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers = 36 | Initial **Average** = 45

Numbers to be **discarded** = 37 and 53

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of Observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eac8563fc0f52bba10a1ad2f825db5b91d4c010f77849666f1e581df80c83885.png] 

**Calculations:**

questions.question: The average salary of all the workers in a factory is ₹14,000. The average salary of 80 skilled workers is ₹15,000 and the average salary of the remaining workers is ₹12,000. Find the total number of workers in the factory.

Apply the **Alligation Method** between **Skilled** and **Remaining** workers.

Ratio of **Skilled : Remaining** = (14,000 − 12,000) : (15,000 − 14,000) = 2,000 : 1,000 = **2 : 1**.

According to the question, 2 units = **80 workers** → 1 unit = **40 workers**.

Total workers = (2 + 1) units = 3 units = 3 × 40 = **120**.

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

⇒ 14,000T = (15,000 × 80) + 12,000(T − 80)

⇒ 14,000T = 1,200,000 + 12,000T − 960,000

⇒ 14,000T − 12,000T = 240,000

⇒ 2,000T = 240,000

⇒ T = 240,000 ÷ 2,000

⇒ T = **120**

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

questions.question: The sum of five numbers is 655. The average of the first two numbers is 77 and the third number is 102. Find the average of the remaining two numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Sum of remaining 2 numbers** = 655 − (2 × 77) − 102

⇒ 655 − 154 − 102 = 399

**Average** = 399 ÷ 2 = 199.5

**∴ The correct answer is 199.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sum of **5 numbers** = 655

Average of **first 2 numbers** = 77

Value of the **3rd number** = 102

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c0570caa88ed236cab3cd6c81ed851605b12cc688458f0244372d780c1834135.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of first 2 numbers = Average × Count = 77 × 2 = 154

⇒ Sum of first 3 numbers = (Sum of first 2) + (3rd number) = 154 + 102 = 256

⇒ Sum of remaining 2 numbers = (Total sum) − (Sum of first 3) = 655 − 256 = 399

⇒ Average of remaining 2 numbers = (Sum of remaining 2) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 399 ÷ 2 = 199.5

**∴ The correct answer is 199.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Average

The **Arithmetic Mean** or average is the ratio of the sum of all values to the total number of values. Formula: **Avg = Total Sum ÷ n**.

Sum of Observations

If the average and the number of observations are known, the total sum is calculated as: **Sum = Average × Number of terms**.

Weighted Average

When groups with different averages are combined, the total average is **(n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)**.</p

questions.question: A vendor sells 8, 12, 10, 14, and 6 mangoes over five days. What is the average number of mangoes sold per day?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **Average** is simply the sum of all values divided by the total number of items.

Sum = 8 + 12 + 10 + 14 + 6 = 50

Total Days = 5

Average = 50 ÷ 5 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10 mangoes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Mangoes sold over five days are **8, 12, 10, 14, and 6**.

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08040b002dd3246a6e390717e448aecaa256cdd2bd287c9f5438d6c51d808b4c.png] 

⇒ Sum of mangoes = 8 + 12 + 10 + 14 + 6

⇒ Total sum = 50

⇒ Total number of days = 5

⇒ Average per day = 50 ÷ 5

⇒ Average per day = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10 mangoes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

It is the most common type of average, calculated by dividing the sum of values by the count of values (n).

Weighted Average

When different items have different importance, the average is ∑(wᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ ∑wᵢ.

Change in Average

If a constant 'k' is added to every observation in a set, the new average will be the old average + k.</p

questions.question: A company produces two products A and B with prices of ₹156 and ₹220, respectively. If 55% of the products sold are A and 45% of the products sold are B. Find the weighted average price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of quantities of **Product A** and **Product B** = 55 : 45 = 11 : 9.

Weighted Average Price = [(PriceA × RatioA) + (PriceB × RatioB)] ÷ Total Ratio

⇒ (156 × 11 + 220 × 9) ÷ (11 + 9)

⇒ (1716 + 1980) ÷ 20 = 3696 ÷ 20 = 184.80.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹184.80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of **Product A** (P₁) = ₹156 | Weight (w₁) = 55%

Price of **Product B** (P₂) = ₹220 | Weight (w₂) = 45%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c7891accfecc3b7cee486099389536624fa62a8232e88b9c660a565c0dc0d75.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (P₁w₁ + P₂w₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Weighted Average = (156 × 55 + 220 × 45) ÷ 100

⇒ Weighted Average = (8580 + 9900) ÷ 100

⇒ Weighted Average = 18480 ÷ 100

⇒ Weighted Average = ₹184.80

**∴ The correct answer is ₹184.80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

Unlike a simple average, the **weighted average** accounts for the relative importance or frequency of each value in the data set.

Deviation Method for Averages

Assume a base average (e.g., 156) and calculate the **net deviation** from the other values multiplied by their weights to find the adjustment.

Ratio in Averages

When percentages are given, you can simplify them into their **lowest ratio** form to make the calculations easier without changing the final result.

questions.question: The average score of 10 players was initially recorded as 55. However, it was later discovered that a score of 84 had been mistakenly read as 48. Determine the correct average score.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net change in **total score** = Correct score − Wrong score = 84 − 48 = +36.

Change in **average** = Net change ÷ Number of players = 36 ÷ 10 = +3.6.

Correct average = Initial average + Change in average = 55 + 3.6 = 58.6.

**∴ The correct answer is 58.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial average of **10 players** = 55

Incorrectly recorded score = 48

Actual correct score = 84

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of items

Correct Sum = (Initial Average × n) − Wrong Value + Correct Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c914870757aafd3a378247313a602331c72b788ba1bec7e948b8d3319109546c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Total Sum = 10 × 55 = 550

⇒ Correct Total Sum = 550 − 48 + 84

⇒ Correct Total Sum = 502 + 84 = 586

⇒ Correct Average = 586 ÷ 10

⇒ Correct Average = 58.6

**∴ The correct answer is 58.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Correction Rule

When one or more values are incorrectly recorded, the new average can be calculated using New Average = Old Average + [(Correct Value − Incorrect Value) ÷ Total Number of Items].

Net Deviation

The sum of deviations of all observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero. In correction problems, the net deviation is simply the difference between the correct and incorrect values.

Combined Average

If two groups with n₁ and n₂ items have averages a₁ and a₂, the combined average is (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p
